da.consejo: Preposition of temporary origin and duration.

eccolo.en: There it is; here it comes.

texto: It is equivalent to the Spanish formulas «since...» or «llevar + gerundio»: **Vivo qui da tre anni** (I have lived here for three years / I have been living here for three years); **Studio l'italiano da sei mesi** (Italian study for six months).
Attention! The past is not used, because the action remains open and in force at the time it is spoken.
To ask how long a current action lasts, **Da quanto tempo...?**: **Da quanto tempo abiti a Roma?** is said (How long have you been living in Rome?).

filas: Da quanto tempo vivi a Milano?
Vivo a Milano da due anni.

frases.it: Da quanto tempo vivi a Roma, Luca?
frases.es: ¿Desde hace cuánto tiempo vives en Roma, Luca?
frases.en: How long have you been living in Rome, Luca?

frases.it: Vivo qui da tre anni, mi piace molto!
frases.es: Vivo aquí desde hace tres años, ¡me gusta mucho!
frases.en: I've been living here for three years, I like it a lot!

frases.it: Studio italiano da sei mesi e lavoro qui da gennaio.
frases.es: Estudio italiano desde hace seis meses y trabajo aquí desde enero.
frases.en: I've been studying Italian for six months and I've been working here since January.

frases.it: Bravo! E da quanto tempo aspetti l'autobus?
frases.es: ¡Bravo! ¿Y desde hace cuánto tiempo esperas el autobús?
frases.en: Bravo! And how long have you been waiting for the bus?
analisis: for how long you've been waiting

frases.es: Espero desde hace diez minutos. ¡Ahí está!
frases.en: I've been waiting for ten minutes. There he is!
analisis: I've been waiting for ten minutes.

bloques.pregunta: What verbal time is used in Italian for an action initiated in the past that continues today?

opciones.explicacion: The present construction + «da» states that the situation is still open today.
It would indicate a closed and concluded fact, incompatible with present validity.
It indicates a coming action that has not yet begun.

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «for two months» in Italian?

opciones.explicacion: The «da» preposition precedes the period of time to indicate current duration.
«Fa» indicates time spent for a finished past fact («Two months ago»).
«Per» delimits a closed duration in the past or future, not an existing action.
«Da» + duration with present indicates that I continue to study today.
It does not express the continued validity from an initial point of view.
«Fa» is postponed to the number and expresses an event concluded in the past.

bloques.pregunta: What does the person who speaks communicate?

opciones.texto: He began studying Italian in January and continues to study it now.
opciones.explicacion: «Da» marks the time of start of an existing action.

opciones.texto: He studied Italian only during the month of January and he already left him.
opciones.explicacion: It would indicate an action concluded in the past.

opciones.texto: He will begin his Italian classes next January.
opciones.explicacion: It combines the past starting point with a future plan.

bloques.frase: Da quanto tempo lavori a Milano?

opciones.texto: How long have you been working in Milan so far?
opciones.explicacion: She asked about the accumulated duration of a current work activity.

opciones.texto: What year did you finish your job in Milan?
opciones.explicacion: I would ask for the end of a completed stage.

opciones.texto: What time do you get out of work in Milan on Fridays?
opciones.explicacion: I would ask for a schedule, not for the duration in years or months.

bloques.frase: Vivo a Roma da tre anni
bloques.traduccion: I've been living in Rome for three years.
bloques.explicacion: Temporary construction of present with the «da» preposition.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the verb in the right present.
bloques.frase: ___ qui da sei mesi e mi piace la città. (io)

opciones.explicacion: «Abito» in present indicates that I continue to reside in the city.
I would indicate that I lived in the past but no longer live there.
I would present the stay as a closed period.

intro: To indicate how long you've been doing something that still continues in the present, the Italian uses «da» with present.
